Class GraphExpander

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.GraphExpander
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Task
public class GraphExpander extends Object implements edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Task
A graph expander manages the generation of a story graph from a Tandem Tales logical story world, serving as a central point for many node expanding threads to report their work and ensuring that nodes are generated in a deterministic order.

This process can be given a maximum depth to expand the graph. A max depth of 1 means it will generate all states which can be reached by taking up to 1 action from the initial state. A max depth of 2 means it will generate all states which can be reached by taking up to 2 actions from the initial state, and so on. The last layer of nodes generated by this method will still have outgoing temporal edges, but only if they lead to nodes generated earlier in the process (i.e. nodes at a lower depth). In other words, if this process runs with a max depth of 5, it mean the graph will include any state which can be reached by a sequence of up to 5 actions from the initial state, and from those nodes it is still possible to move to other states to, but only of those states were also generated at depth 5 or lower.

If this process runs without a max depth, it will run until all reachable states have been generated. Assuming the graph is finite, it will eventually halt.

This object's synchronized methods ensure that, while many threads might be running simultaneously to expand nodes, only one thread at a time is modifying the story graph. This object also ensures that nodes are expanded in order of their IDs, meaning this procedure will always produce the same story graph despite the non-determinism introduced by concurrency.

While many threads can be working to expand nodes at once, because they must all coordinate with this object to add new nodes to the graph, the speedup from running many threads is minimal.

Author:
Stephen G. Ware
